clue.text: Drink distributed in eastern US

indicators.note: letters distributed are spread about and dealt out afresh, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drink being sold across the eastern United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' shuffles the nine letters of EASTERN US; 'in' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white wine from Bordeaux, so it is a drink.

clue.text: A little way along, discards a bothersome item of footwear

indicators.note: A little way along says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone a short way down the road throws away an annoying shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, worn especially by French peasants, so a kind of shoe.

clue.text: Unqualified — a new Church statement

parts.note: unqualified as in complete or absolute, like utter
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church issues an absolute new statement of doctrine.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is something spoken, a remark or declaration.

clue.text: President is in from France — what's brought about that? Force ignored at start

indicators.note: something brought about another is placed around it, so the exclamation wraps the preceding letters

parts.note: EH is the exclamation 'what?', what's being read as 'what is'
taken as written
EN is the French word for in

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for force is ignored, dropping its opening letter

parts.note: power is force or might

explanation.surface: A puzzled observer asks what has caused a president to arrive from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's' is read as the puzzled exclamation 'what?', and 'brought about that' means wrapped around the French-tinged letters before it; 'ignored at start' cuts the opening letter of the word for force.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight D. Eisenhower was the 34th President of the United States.

clue.text: Beginning northern climb

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: Starting the climb up the northern face of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into being, an adjective sense of beginning.

clue.text: One with potential beginning to entertain the French

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a beginning is a start
LE is French for the

explanation.surface: A promising performer starts out by entertaining French audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A starlet is a young actress tipped for future stardom, someone with promise.

clue.text: Officer at sea bawling out sailor upsets newcomers at start

indicators.note: only the start of each of the following words is taken, their opening letters

explanation.surface: A ship's officer shouting at a sailor alarms the new recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun, or boatswain, is the ship's officer in charge of equipment and crew.

clue.text: Mixture of, oddly, barley and whiskey

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters, the first, third and fifth, are taken

parts.note: Whiskey is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for W

explanation.surface: A drink blended from barley and whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: A brew is a concoction or mixture, often of drinks prepared together.

clue.text: It might be buttered in historic Scottish place

definitions.meaning: a small baked cake often split and buttered
... in Perthshire is where Scottish kings were crowned on the Stone of ...

explanation.surface: Something buttered in an old Scottish town.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share a spelling: a teatime bake, and the ancient Scottish royal coronation site.

clue.text: Yet to iron slips, getting reputation?

indicators.note: letters that slip slide out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who has yet to iron their slips worries about their good name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips' looks like underwear waiting to be ironed but is the anagram signal; the question mark flags that notoriety is a bad reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, an unfavourable kind of reputation.

clue.text: Club has outside somewhere to swim

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport

indicators.note: only the outside of the word, its first and last letters, is taken

explanation.surface: A sports club boasts a pool on its grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Public baths are a swimming pool building, a place for swimming.

clue.text: One unfairly blamed is rested, inspiring better English attempt

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the other letters are taken inside

parts.note: to rest on a seat is to sit, past tense sat
to cap something is to better or outdo it
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A sidelined player who has been rested is spurred to make a better English attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is a person made to bear the blame for others' faults.

clue.text: Aren't at all trained for dance

indicators.note: trained letters are shaped or drilled into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some people are not trained at all for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a fast whirling Italian folk dance.

clue.text: Successor of Ambassador, Irish

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: The successor to an Irish ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is one who succeeds to a title or estate.

clue.text: New bar pianist widely supported

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is made, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A new pianist in the bar has broad backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bipartisan measure has the backing of both main parties, so broad support.

clue.text: Partner kind with prisoner

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
a kind is a sort

explanation.surface: A prisoner's partner is a kind person.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse or companion, especially of a monarch.

clue.text: Pass over worker scoffing one breakfast item?

indicators.note: scoffing means eating up, so one piece is swallowed inside the other

parts.note: to cross is to pass over
I is the Roman numeral for one
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A worker wolfs one item at breakfast as he passes by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffing' puts the numeral one inside the word for pass over. The question mark admits this is only one possible breakfast item.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a flaky crescent roll typically eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: First loch to feature in article — it's emblematic

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: the is the definite article
1ST is written for first, the 1 read as the letter I
L is a map abbreviation for loch

explanation.surface: The leading loch appears in a magazine article as a symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' gives 1ST with the numeral read as I. 'to feature in' puts ISTL inside THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The thistle is the national emblem of Scotland, so it is emblematic.

clue.text: Four identical notes about a private conversation?

indicators.note: the notes go about the letter, wrapping around it

parts.note: TE is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, written four times

explanation.surface: A musical phrase of four repeated notes about a secret chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A in the middle of TETE TETE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private talk between two people, French for head to head.

clue.text: Finished first helpings of everything at table? Pig!

parts.note: over means finished or ended

indicators.note: the first helpings of the words are their opening letters only

explanation.surface: Someone finished first and then took a second helping of everything on the table: a pig!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig!' is a verb here, to pig out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig is to eat greedily, so to stuff oneself beyond need.

clue.text: They might poke fun at posers?

definitions.meaning: a poser is a puzzling question, and so is a teaser

explanation.surface: Mockers who might laugh at show-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posers' looks like people striking poses, but it is the puzzle sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: teasers mock people, and brain-teasers are tricky puzzles.

clue.text: Eerie with first appearance of antipathy for love? Horrible!

indicators.note: for means one letter is put in place of another, a swap

parts.note: ghostly means eerie
love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: the first appearance of the word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An eerie dislike instead of love: how horrible!
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the O in GHOSTLY for A from antipathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghastly means horrible or shockingly unpleasant.

clue.text: Brilliance of ultimately charming new arrivals?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a litter is a batch of newborn animals

explanation.surface: The brilliance of some delightful newborns.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags new arrivals as newborn puppies or kittens.
explanation.definitionFit: Glitter is sparkle, a dazzling shine.

clue.text: Disadvantage of small horse

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: The drawback of a little horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hitch or drawback.

clue.text: Place to walk one's going to by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: I'LL, short for I will, means I am going to

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they will walk somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats, a walkway.

clue.text: After graduate comes to essential point, assess court official

indicators.note: After means the next piece follows the graduate in the answer

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts graduate
the gist is the essential point
to rate is to assess

explanation.surface: Once a graduate gets to the crux, a court official must assess it.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a judicial officer who hears cases in a lower court.

clue.text: Contest on equal footing over time

parts.note: level or even

explanation.surface: A competition fairly balanced over time.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a sporting competition, a contest.

clue.text: Meander, getting trade maybe

definitions.meaning: a trade ... is one kind of ...

explanation.surface: Wandering about and picking up some business.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the verb, twisting along; and the noun, air currents such as trade winds.

clue.text: Avoiding pub maybe, not present to receive money

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the money goes inside

parts.note: absent means not present
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone skipping the pub, not there to collect cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin' is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinent means refraining from drink, so a teetotaller avoids the pub.

clue.text: At audition rocked in leather

indicators.note: audition is hearing, so the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: swayed means rocked from side to side

explanation.surface: A performer at an audition rocking out in leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped surface.

clue.text: Review of rent day to be widely discussed online

indicators.note: a review re-views and revises, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rent review day becomes a hot topic on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: To trend is to become a popular topic on social media.

clue.text: Tough owner's horses, not half-decent

parts.note: a string is the set of racehorses belonging to one owner or stable

indicators.note: not half says only half of the word stays, here its closing portion

explanation.surface: An owner's racehorses that are not even half-decent are a tough prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: In horse racing a string is the set of racehorses kept by one owner or stable.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent means strict or rigorous, demanding.
